intro: This branch teaches classic constructions: drawing exact figures with only a compass and an unmarked straightedge (ruler with no measurements). Each one is then shown to work, by putting construction or proof steps in order, picking the reason, or working out a length or angle the construction creates.

V.15.01.what: Using a compass to copy a length or an angle exactly, without measuring.

levels.a: Understands that a compass carries a length: a copied arc has the same length.
levels.b: Puts in order the steps for copying segments, such as building one as long as two others combined.
levels.c: Puts in order the steps for copying an angle.
levels.d: Picks the reason the copied angle is equal: the triangles match side-side-side (SSS).

V.15.02.what: Constructing the line that cuts a segment exactly in half at a right angle (its perpendicular bisector).

levels.a: Knows the compass must open more than half the segment for the arcs to meet.
levels.b: Uses the construction to find the midpoint.
levels.c: Uses the right angle the construction makes to find a missing angle.
levels.d: Puts the lines of a proof that the construction works in order.

V.15.03.what: Constructing the line that cuts an angle exactly in half (its bisector).

levels.a: Works out lengths made by the first arc across both sides of the angle.
levels.b: Recognizes the kite shape the construction arcs create.
levels.c: Uses the bisector to find the two equal half angles.
levels.d: Puts the lines of a proof that the construction works in order.

V.15.04.what: Constructing a line at a right angle to a given line, through a chosen point.

levels.a: Finds lengths made by the first arc, drawn around a point that lies on the line.
levels.b: Works out the distance to the line when the point is off the line.
levels.c: Puts the construction steps in order.
levels.d: Picks the reason the construction gives a right angle.

V.15.05.what: Constructing a line through a point that runs parallel to a given line.

levels.a: Knows the method copies an angle to make matching (corresponding) angles equal.
levels.b: Puts the construction steps in order.
levels.c: Orders the steps of another method: two perpendiculars in a row make a parallel line.
levels.d: Picks the reason the new line is parallel.

V.15.06.what: Constructing a regular hexagon and an equilateral triangle inside a circle by stepping the radius around it.

levels.a: Finds the angle at the center made by one radius-length step.
levels.b: Uses the fact that the hexagon's sides equal the radius.
levels.c: Finds the exact side of the triangle made by joining every other point.
levels.d: Picks the reason each step makes a 60 degree angle at the center.
levels.e: Uses circle angle facts to find angles inside the hexagon.
levels.f: Finds the exact area of one point of the six-pointed star made by two triangles.

V.15.07.what: Constructing a square inside a circle using two diameters that cross at right angles.

levels.a: Draws a diameter, a line through the center from edge to edge.
levels.b: Puts in order the steps for a second diameter at a right angle to the first.
levels.c: Joins the four ends and finds the square's exact side.
levels.d: Picks why the shape made must be a square.

V.15.08.what: Constructing the lines from an outside point that just touch a circle (tangents).

levels.a: Finds the midpoint between the point and the circle's center.
levels.b: Finds the radius of the helper circle drawn on that segment.
levels.c: Finds a tangent's length, using the right angle where it touches.
levels.d: Uses the right angle in a half circle to find missing angles.
levels.e: Finds the area of the kite formed by both tangents and two radii.
levels.f: Finds the length of a tangent shared by two circles.

V.15.09.what: Constructing the circle that passes through a triangle's three corners, and the circle that fits snugly inside it.

levels.a: Finds where the perpendicular bisectors meet, the center of the outside circle.
levels.b: Finds the radius of the outside circle.
levels.c: Uses the fact that the angle bisectors meet at a point equally far from all three sides.
levels.d: Finds the radius of the inside circle from the area.
levels.e: Uses circle angle facts to find an angle at the outside circle's center.
levels.f: Finds a triangle's area from where its inside circle touches the longest side.
